recognize_zh: 骨髓切片免疫染色顯示骨小樑旁緻密的紡錘形細胞聚集，胞質強陽性（肥大細胞標記）；臨床照片中前臂皮膚刮擦後出現線狀紅色風疹塊（Darier's sign），伴散在紅棕色斑丘疹，符合肥大細胞增生症。
features: Bone marrow biopsy immunostain: dense paratrabecular and perivascular aggregate of spindle-shaped cells with strong cytoplasmic positivity
Aggregated positive cells form a compact multifocal infiltrate adjacent to bone trabeculae, with scattered negative hematopoietic cells and fat
Clinical photo: linear erythematous urticarial wheal along the stroked skin of the forearm (Darier's sign)
Scattered small reddish-brown macules/papules on the arm consistent with urticaria pigmentosa-type skin lesions
describe_en: The bone marrow core biopsy immunostained for a mast cell marker (likely tryptase or CD117) shows a dense, compact paratrabecular infiltrate of spindle-shaped positive cells forming aggregates well in excess of 15 cells, with residual hematopoiesis and fat. The clinical photograph demonstrates a linear urticarial wheal and flare after stroking of the forearm skin (Darier's sign), with scattered pigmented maculopapular lesions. Findings are consistent with systemic mastocytosis with cutaneous involvement; CD25/CD2 aberrant expression, KIT D816V mutation and serum tryptase support the diagnosis.

ddx.vs: Reactive mast cells are scattered, round and interstitial without dense spindle-cell aggregates or CD25 expression.
Fibroblasts are spindle-shaped but tryptase- and CD117-negative.
HCL infiltrates are CD20/annexin A1-positive B cells with fried-egg appearance rather than tryptase-positive spindle cells.
Simple dermatographism arises from normal skin, whereas Darier's sign is elicited on pigmented mastocytosis lesions with increased dermal mast cells.

stain: IHC: mast cell marker (tryptase/CD117); clinical photo
